correctness.rationale: I enumerated independent subsets by checking pair separation in coordinate differences for all subsets of sizes 1–6; none of size six exist, so no larger subsets exist. I decoded and validated the supplied matching against the 1410 nonempty faces and all 4550 covers, including disjointness, codimension one, and exhaustion of faces by matched and critical cells. Depth-first cycle detection confirms acyclicity with exactly one critical vertex and 141 critical three-simplices. By the acyclic face-poset matching theorem for a finite simplicial complex this gives a CW model with just those cells; each attaching map S²→point is constant, yielding the integral wedge. Independently, a row with two kings forces neighboring rows empty; the two remaining adjacent rows use pairwise separated, distinct columns and hence hold at most two kings together. A five-set must then occupy every row with successive differences ±2 modulo 5; all signs coincide from closure after five steps. The ten resulting lines are the only possible invariant nonempty faces for a nonidentity order-five translation. The five invariant lines in each distinguished direction contribute +5 in degree four (a 5-cycle has sign +1); the reduced augmentation contributes −1 in every case. Alternating trace therefore gives 141, −4 and 1 on the specified classes in H_3, also checked from permutation cycles on all faces. An equivariant barycentric subdivision has no inversions on simplices (a stabilizer preserves each face in the chain by dimension), so quotient chains are coinvariants. Over Q these identify with invariants by averaging, which is exact; the character averages give 25 (two lines), 29 (four lines) and 5 (full group). No integral quotient assertion follows. evidence: The target is the degree-8 king torus. The five-by-five Cartesian hard-square record 374b6b4d37f7 has degree 4; the triangular record fddbdcaa38d0 has degree 6.

The graph complement has degree 16; equivalently its clique complex is the independence complex of the king torus. Using the self-complementarity of C5, the complement is a disjunctive cycle square, not a Cartesian square or the king graph itself.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Complement/clique terminology changes the representation of the complex, not the invariant, and a single C5 self-complementarity cannot identify the two different degree-8 and degree-16 graphs. The two adjacent periodic lattice results are about different graphs, not aliases of the target.

value.rationale: This small doubly periodic strong product is a natural exact test case distinct from rectangular path products. The integral wedge supplies attaching-map, concentration and torsion information absent from enumeration. The actual translation character resolves which slopes differ and gives rational homology of both nonfree and free subgroup quotients. These are meaningful exact refinements, not a re-tabulation of the known Euler characteristic.
